name: Eplerenone

lead: Eplerenone is an aldosterone blocker that forum users discuss mainly as a pricier alternative to spironolactone, sometimes with water retention and puffiness in mind.

It blocks the mineralocorticoid receptor so aldosterone cannot drive sodium retention and potassium loss, and it is more receptor-selective than spironolactone. It is approved for hypertension and for heart failure after a heart attack, where the EPHESUS and EMPHASIS-HF trials tested it. Two looksmax.org threads mention it, mostly about cost, and no study has tested it for puffiness.

paras: It is a prescription tablet taken on a schedule set by a doctor for heart failure or blood pressure. In forum discussion it is raised as an option for people who want an aldosterone blocker without spironolactone.
The label's main concern is high potassium and raised creatinine, with higher risk in kidney disease, diabetes and when taken with certain interacting drugs. It is prescription-only in the US.

angle.text: Eplerenone comes up on forums mainly as a costly spironolactone alternative for people who want an aldosterone blocker, sometimes with water retention in mind. By blocking aldosterone it reduces sodium and water retention. It is approved for heart failure and hypertension, with no appearance studies.

lead: Eplerenone (brand name Inspra) is a selective aldosterone receptor antagonist and potassium-sparing diuretic. The US label lists two indications: improving survival in stable adults with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction after a myocardial infarction, and treating hypertension. [1][2]

It is catalogued on the wiki as a spironolactone alternative under depuffing. Two looksmax.org threads mention it, mostly about its cost and where to obtain it; no published study has tested eplerenone for facial puffiness or other appearance outcomes. [3][4]
Its best-evidenced uses are cardiovascular: the EPHESUS and EMPHASIS-HF trials tested it in heart failure. [5][6] Labelled risks center on hyperkalemia. [2]

paras: The label indicates eplerenone to improve survival in stable adults with symptomatic HFrEF after acute myocardial infarction and to lower blood pressure in adults. [2] An American Heart Association scientific statement discusses mineralocorticoid antagonists in resistant hypertension, [7] and a European Heart Journal review traces the development of steroidal and nonsteroidal antagonists. [8]

Eplerenone binds the mineralocorticoid receptor and blocks aldosterone, which acts in epithelial tissues such as the kidney and non-epithelial tissues such as the heart, blood vessels and brain. [2] Grokipedia says it is more selective for this receptor than spironolactone and causes fewer sex-hormone-related effects such as gynecomastia, which is one reason it is discussed as a spironolactone alternative. [1]

The label lists hyperkalemia and increased creatinine as the most common adverse reactions in the post-infarction heart failure population, with higher hyperkalemia risk in renal impairment, diabetes, proteinuria, and with ACE inhibitors, ARBs, NSAIDs and moderate CYP3A inhibitors. [2] Pregnancy case reports are insufficient to establish risk, and animal studies showed no developmental effects. [2]

In two looksmax.org threads, users discuss eplerenone's price per month at a 25 mg strength and compare it with other products and sources; commenters disagree on what it should cost. [3][4] The threads do not present studies of eplerenone for appearance.

No studies found on eplerenone for facial puffiness or cosmetic uses. Large trials concern heart disease: EPHESUS randomised patients with left ventricular dysfunction after myocardial infarction, and EMPHASIS-HF randomised 2,737 patients with NYHA class II systolic heart failure; both are cited as supporting its approved use. [5][6] The 4E study compared eplerenone, enalapril and their combination in hypertension with left ventricular hypertrophy, [9] and a randomised study compared finerenone with eplerenone in worsening heart failure with diabetes or kidney disease. [10]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, eplerenone appears in a small number of threads about cost and acquisition. [3][4]
